name: Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia-Bowed Forearms-Facial Dysmorphism Syndrome
aliases: SMD with Bowed Forearms and Facial Dysmorphism
Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia Type with Forearm Bowing and Craniofacial Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia-Bowed Forearms-Facial Dysmorphism Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral bowed forearms with metaphyseal abnormalities
Characteristic facial dysmorphic features including midface hypoplasia, depressed nasal bridge, and hypertelorism
Spondylodysplasia with platyspondyly and irregular vertebral endplates on imaging
Postnatal growth retardation with short stature
Metaphyseal irregularities and flaring in long bones on radiographs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: bowed forearms with metaphyseal abnormalities, characteristic facial dysmorphism, and spinal abnormalities on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always conclusive due to limited data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral bowed forearms with metaphyseal dysplasia
searchTerms: bowed forearms with bone growth issues
curved lower arms with metaphyseal abnormalities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphism including midface hypoplasia and depressed nasal bridge
searchTerms: distinct facial features with flat midface
depressed nasal bridge and flat face

common.symptomName: Short stature due to postnatal growth retardation
searchTerms: short height from slow growth after birth
below average height due to growth retardation

common.symptomName: Metaphyseal flaring and irregularities in long bones
searchTerms: widened and uneven long bone ends
flared and irregular bone growth areas

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in forearm joints

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications secondary to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: breathing issues due to chest wall deformities
respiratory problems from rib cage abnormalities

imaging: Radiographs showing metaphyseal dysplasia with flaring and irregularities
Platyspondyly and irregular vertebral endplates on spinal X-rays
Bowing of the radius and ulna bilaterally
genetic: Mutations in genes related to skeletal development (specific gene not definitively identified)
other: Clinical diagnosis primarily based on phenotype and radiological findings

distinguishingFeatures: Different facial features without midface hypoplasia
Distinct metaphyseal corner fractures on imaging

redFlags: Severe bowing of forearms causing functional impairment
Progressive spinal deformities leading to neurological compromise
Failure to thrive or severe growth retardation
references: Orphanet: Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia-Bowed Forearms-Facial Dysmorphism Syndrome (ORPHA:168552)
